title: A Signed Note App with a Backdoor in app.asar, Reused Across Campaigns
subtitle: A ClickFix paste delivers the real, vendor-signed flomo app. The backdoor is in app.asar, which the signature doesn't cover.

meta.v: Same app.asar as a public May case
The stager script and any tasking

nodes.label: ClickFix paste
nodes.sub: irm | iex with a gated user agent and header
nodes.desc: The pasted command fetches a script with a fake Windows-Update user agent and a header that both carry the same token, which reads like a gate that only answers the right client.

nodes.label: Stager script
nodes.sub: Not captured, so the ZIP download step is unseen
nodes.desc: I have the original command and the ZIP it led to, but not the script the stager domain served, so I can't show which step fetches the ZIP.
nodes.notes: Open. A copy of what xorados[.]com returns to the right user agent and header would confirm this step.

nodes.label: Signed flomo app
nodes.sub: Every exe verifies; the backdoor is in app.asar
nodes.desc: flomo.exe and its six DLLs all verify against their signatures and show the vendor's EV certificate. The malware is in resources/app.asar, the Electron main-process bundle, which the PE signature never covered. I recomputed the Authenticode digest for all seven PE files.
nodes.notes: The app.asar hash matches a public write-up from May: same build, different stager and campaign tag. flomo.exe itself is the vendor's own, so don't blocklist it.

nodes.label: 30-second beacon
nodes.sub: POST to finework[.]top/api/, cert checks off
nodes.desc: A loop in background.js POSTs [id, COMPUTERNAME, USERNAME, tag] every 30 seconds. The id is a random 8-character string kept in setup.txt. The tag comes from a readme.txt beside the exe, here kdh-main, which matches the ZIP's name.
nodes.notes: The tag changes per campaign, which makes it the best pivot between campaigns.

nodes.label: Run JS or drop an EXE
nodes.sub: A task is eval'd, or written to %TEMP% and run
nodes.desc: The injected function takes a task from the reply and either evals its e field or writes its files map, base64-decoded, into %TEMP%\<millisecond timestamp>\ and runs the .exe among them.
nodes.notes: Read from the code. Open: I have no host telemetry, so I can't say what the operator tasked.
